sentences.text: Only one species, V. exxoni, is known for this genus.
This dinosaur is estimated to have measured 5.6 meters in length.
The genus name derives from the Latin terms via, meaning road, and venator, meaning hunter.
The specific name honors the Exxon oil company for contributing funding to the excavations.
The fossil consists of a partial skeleton including the skull.
The spinous processes of the caudal vertebrae and other vertebrae widen at the extreme top in lateral view to an axe-like shape.
The genus was formally described in 2016 by Filippi and colleagues.
The type and only known species, V. exxoni, was described and named in 2016 by Leonardo Sebastián Filippi, Ariel Hernán Méndez, Rubén Darío Juárez Valieri, and Alberto Carlos Garrido.
The holotype fossil, cataloged as MAU-Pv-LI 530, was found at the La Invernada site in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
Viavenator possessed a brain morphology and inner ear similar to the South American abelisaurid Aucasaurus.
Compared to Majungasaurus, Viavenator relied more on quick head movements and sophisticated gaze stabilization mechanisms.
Viavenator is classified as a member of the family Abelisauridae.
Viavenator is a member of the clade Brachyrostra and occupies a basal position within the smaller clade Furileusauria.
Filippi et al. classified Viavenator into the new clade Furileusauria, which also includes Carnotaurus.
Viavenator lived in the Santonian-aged Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina.
Viavenator lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 86 to 83 million years ago in the Santonian.
Viavenator lived from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian.
